findings.evidence: M4.34 added GroupEvent::MemberLeft so a group losing its leader mid-sync reopens the join barrier; M4.43 added SyncGroups::refuse/Known::Refused so followers already parked are released when no assignment is coming. `grep -rn '\.refuse(' crates/oqueue-broker/src/` outside tests returns two lines, both sync_group.rs:219 and :230 inside submit_assignment. Heartbeats::leave, Heartbeats::sweep and AllMembersGone therefore reopen the barrier in the coordinator while the cell keeps holding nothing. Probed: seat m1,m2 at CompletingRebalance@1, park m2 on the barrier, have m1 leave via Heartbeats::leave -- state=PreparingRebalance gen=1, follower not released, error_code=-1 after waited_ms=3000000. durability.rs's a_parked_follower_is_woken_when_its_leaders_submission_is_refused proves the release works on the one path that was wired.
findings.summary: SyncGroups::refuse is called only from submit_assignment, so every other route out of CompletingRebalance strands the followers parked on the barrier

findings.evidence: join_group/mod.rs:120-132 changed the structurally identical arm away from this code and wrote the reason out: 'UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR is not retriable in the Java consumer, which raises it out of poll()'. barrier.rs:112-119, barrier.rs:83-89, join_group/mod.rs:221-223 and generations.rs:116-123 each state the same rule. Probed: seat m1,m2 at CompletingRebalance@1, park m2, submit nothing -- error_code=-1 waited_ms=3000000. Reachable with nothing wrong, by M4.47's route and by a leader dying between JoinBarrierComplete and its SyncGroup. check-fencing-seam.sh covers Refusal's six codes and UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR is not one, so nothing enforces the convention.
findings.summary: sync_group.rs:108 answers UNKNOWN_SERVER_ERROR where every sibling give-up arm in the group protocol answers REBALANCE_IN_PROGRESS

findings.evidence: scripts/check-mutants.sh:30-31 carries M0.17's oqueue-core-only figure and names its own trigger: 'the day it is not, a nightly schedule is the change rule 16 actually describes'. baselines/mutants.txt:26 says '6-hour'. findings.evidence: group_state.rs:87-93 says the epoch 'Lags GenerationId between a join barrier closing and a sync completing ... so a caller can always tell a rebalance started from a rebalance produced an assignment'. Probed with parked.rs's own interleaving -- a parked generation-1 SyncComplete applied while the group sits at CompletingRebalance@2 -- the record reads state=Stable gen=2 assignment_epoch=2 while no assignment for generation 2 exists or has been submitted. Minor only because grep finds no reader outside group_state.rs, group_coordinator.rs and the actor's own fold; it becomes live the day one exists. Same class as the MemberEpoch claim M4.39 corrected one paragraph above.
findings.summary: AssignmentEpoch's documented invariant is falsifiable and nothing reads it

findings.evidence: barrier.rs:177-204 and :218-248 both take the entries lock, or_default the entry, take the assignments lock, evaluate a generation guard, write an Assignment, drop both and notify_waiters. The difference is Some(map) versus None and one disjunct. The guards deliberately disagree at equality in opposite directions and must be reasoned about as a pair, which a single publish(group, generation, Option<map>) with one predicate would make checkable in one place. Each half is individually pinned by durability.rs:203-314, so this is shape rather than defect.
findings.summary: submit and refuse are a thirty-line duplicate of one lock/guard/write/notify dance, and the guards are the part that took four commits to get right

findings.evidence: roadmap.md:76 says M5 has 20 tasks; `grep -c '^[0-9]\+\. '` on M5.md is 21 after M4.32 added task 21, which M4.32 itself recorded against its own commit and closed anyway. M4.md:158-160 still says 'This milestone will make a sizing assumption; write it down' and it did not -- M7.md:180 carries it as 'deferred from M4 and still open here' while roadmap.md's deferred table has no row, which AGENTS.md names as where such an obligation lives. check-mutants.sh:118's comment claims the skip regex is 'Anchored to the line mutants.sh itself emits, not a substring' while the pattern's `.*skip` alternative makes it exactly a substring match. check-mutants.sh:246 harvests ^MISSED only, so an argued entry whose mutant flips to TIMEOUT is reported stale and the note tells the maintainer to delete a live suppression -- and connection.rs:256:17 appears in the full log as both.
